answer: Each identity claims one mesa-rim lagoon basin, locking a 70-credit bond to its key. It files a core from the basin nadir: depth and a sample serial. Auditors recompute the nadir depth from the lagoon bathymetry table and mesa rim elevation; an error over 4 percent or a reused serial burns the bond. First filing costs 36; the kth costs 36+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6030 and 1000 fakes pay 3,033,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-core ring fails: one serial binds one key and one nadir, so a rented core under another key mismatches the table. Honest filers pay 36 once, bond back after audit.
